title: Bogo-Indian Defense: the ideas
line: A bishop check makes White block with a piece, and Black trades it off.

steps.text: White starts by pushing the pawn in front of its queen two squares, into the center.
Bring the knight out. For now it stops White's other center pawn from coming to e4.
Move the pawn in front of your king one square. It opens a path for your bishop.
steps.after: White brings out the other knight first, so a bishop on b4 would pin nothing.

steps.text: Give check with the bishop anyway. White has to block it with a piece.

also.b7b6: That is the Queen's Indian Defense, also sound. This lesson goes on with the check.
also.d7d5: That holds the center with a pawn, also sound. This lesson goes on with the check.

steps.after: This is the Bogo-Indian Defense. White blocks with its bishop.

steps.text: Guard your bishop with the queen. Now Black can take on d2 when it suits.

also.b4d2: Trading at once works too. This lesson goes on with the queen.

steps.text: Bring the other knight out. It hits White's pawn on d4.
Trade the bishops. White's knight takes back on d2, a quieter square than c3.
Move the pawn in front of your queen one square. It gets the next pawn push ready.
Now push the pawn in front of your king two squares.
steps.after: Black has its share of the center.

summary: A bishop check makes White block. Black guards the bishop, trades it when it suits and builds a pawn center.
